statement: In 10 of 29 books with a problem an adult makes the resolution possible (a tickle, an injection, a 'yes', a repairer called, a carpenter's ramp, a grandmother's new bucket, a garden replanted, a scare explained away); in 19 the child, a peer or an animal resolves it.

scope.population: contemporary open-licence picture books: Book Dash (35), African Storybook (2), StoryWeaver: Pratham Books (5), Room to Read (1); 2014-2026

analyst_note:
2026-10-14: Best Friends and An Unexpected Adventure (wordless) reviewed for this claim. Best Friends: the teacher only suggests; a classmate's invitation and the protagonist's own choice resolve it (counterexample). An Unexpected Adventure has no problem to resolve and is not counted.
2026-10-15: Not counted (no problem to resolve): Bathtub Safari, Khumo, Ga Mohana. Book Dash: Zuko supports (Gogo phones a repairer), Come Back Cat and Feathered Friends contradict. African Storybook: Chicken and Millipede supports (Mother Millipede tells him what to do); Bohlale contradicts (Gogo only names what the child already did). StoryWeaver: Monu tames the monsters alone. 2026-10-20: Amo (an adult fixes the mielie problem) supports; Goodnight, Tinku! counters (play tires the pup; his mother only explains).
2026-10-28: +1 support, +7 counter. StoryWeaver: Get Down, Rocky! (Pratham) supports — the carpenter's ramp, the child only begs; The Lost Ball (Room to Read) counters — the boy finds it himself. Book Dash: all six new books with a problem counter (a dog, a peer, a child, or the animal itself); Let's Go Looking has no problem and is not counted. Proposal was declined (product rule: the child resolves); recorded only. Sources of the new works: Book Dash — A Day Out, Who Ate My Hat, Let's Go Looking, Dudu's Hat, Clever Pig, A House for Mouse, Goldfish Genius; StoryWeaver — Get Down, Rocky! (Pratham Books), The Lost Ball (Room to Read, translated from Bangla).
2026-11-13: +3 support (A Trip to the Tap, AAAAAHHH!!!! Mmawe!, Banzi's Busy Bees: all three also flagged passive_protagonist), +4 counter (I Can Do It!: adults are the problem; Play with Me: the child's own play draws the family in; Dance, Khuzwayo, Dance!: two child friends; Alex's Super Medicine: the text gives the choice to the child, the picture shows Mom with the spoon, counted child-resolved). Going Places, Can We Eat a Rainbow? and Sweet Dreams have no problem to resolve and are not counted. Sources of the new works: Book Dash — A Trip to the Tap (2023), Going Places (2025), AAAAAHHH!!!! Mmawe! (2024), Can We Eat a Rainbow? (2026), I Can Do It! (2026), Play with Me (2026), Banzi's Busy Bees (2025), Dance, Khuzwayo, Dance! (2023), Alex's Super Medicine (2022); StoryWeaver — Sweet Dreams (Pratham Books, year not shown).

magicpaper.current: MagicPaper beats favour the child acting (take_charge, find_own_courage)
magicpaper.suggested: No change; record that adult-enabled endings are common in this population, and track agency as the corpus grows.
